note: The Republic of the Congo: nationals of the other CEMAC states (with a biometric passport) enter without a visa for 90 days; nationals of Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, Togo and the UAE get a visa on arrival; everyone else needs a visa from a mission. The exemption announced for all African Union nationals from 1 January 2027 isn't yet in force. Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Embassy in Washington, which says no Congolese visa is issued at any port of entry; that undated line, addressed to applicants in the US, wasn't taken to overrule the visa on arrival Wikipedia reports for ten African states, which stands on its copy with the exemptions.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of the Republic of the Congo
sources.said: Visitors to the Republic of the Congo must obtain a visa from one of the Republic of the Congo diplomatic missions unless they are citizens from one of the visa-exempt countries or citizens who may obtain a visa on arrival. ... Citizens of the following countries who hold a biometric passport may enter the Republic of Congo without a visa for up to 90 days: Cameroon Central African Republic Chad Equatorial Guinea Gabon ... 1 January 2027: All African Union countries. ... Citizens of the following countries may obtain a visa on arrival: Benin Burkina Faso Côte d'Ivoire Mauritania Morocco Niger Rwanda Senegal Togo United Arab Emirates

sources.title: Embassy of the Republic of Congo, Washington: Visa for the Republic of Congo
sources.said: A valid passport is required for all U.S. citizens and foreign nationals entering the Republic of Congo. ... Please be aware that no Congolese visa will be issued at any port of entry in the Republic of Congo. All visa applications should be submitted ...
